title.es: Simulación de una reunión de vecinos

es: Participar en una reunión simulada de vecinos: proponer un compromiso, conceder un punto, expresar una preocupación y discrepar con tacto, y llegar a un acuerdo con plazo evitando el bloqueo.

teaching.en: I'd like to propose a compromise: a small garden next to the school, which would cost less than the original plan and still serve the whole neighbourhood.
teaching.es: Me gustaría proponer una solución intermedia: un pequeño huerto junto a la escuela, que costaría menos que el plan original y aun así serviría a todo el barrio.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd like to propose + nombre: propuesta formal y cortés; a compromise la presenta como un punto medio.
segments: I'd like to propose a compromise: a small garden next to the school, which
would cost less than the original plan and still serve the whole neighbourhood.
teaching.audioText: I'd like to propose a compromise: a small garden next to the school, which would cost less than the original plan and still serve the whole neighbourhood.

teaching.en: Admittedly, it would cost more at first, but I'm convinced it would last longer, so the budget makes sense over ten years.
teaching.es: Es cierto que costaría más al principio, pero estoy convencido de que duraría más, así que el presupuesto tiene sentido a diez años.
teaching.explanationEs: Admittedly concede un punto contrario antes de defender tu idea con but.
segments: Admittedly, it would cost more at first, but I'm convinced it
would last longer, so the budget makes sense over ten years.
teaching.audioText: Admittedly, it would cost more at first, but I'm convinced it would last longer, so the budget makes sense over ten years.

teaching.en: With respect, I see it a little differently, and I'd like to voice a concern about the budget before we go any further.
teaching.es: Con todo respeto, yo lo veo un poco distinto, y me gustaría expresar una preocupación sobre el presupuesto antes de seguir adelante.
teaching.explanationEs: With respect suaviza el desacuerdo; voice a concern presenta la duda como preocupación, no como ataque.
segments: With respect, I see it a little differently, and I'd like to
voice a concern about the budget before we go any further.
teaching.audioText: With respect, I see it a little differently, and I'd like to voice a concern about the budget before we go any further.

teaching.en: The real sticking point is the noise, and if we cannot reach a consensus tonight, we risk a deadlock that helps nobody.
teaching.es: El verdadero punto conflictivo es el ruido, y si no alcanzamos un consenso esta noche, corremos el riesgo de un bloqueo que no ayuda a nadie.
teaching.explanationEs: Sticking point = lo que impide avanzar; consensus = acuerdo de todos; deadlock = nadie cede.
segments: The real sticking point is the noise, and if we cannot
reach a consensus tonight, we risk a deadlock that helps nobody.
teaching.audioText: The real sticking point is the noise, and if we cannot reach a consensus tonight, we risk a deadlock that helps nobody.

teaching.en: Shall we agree to start small and review the cost in June, so that nobody feels they are giving up too much?
teaching.es: ¿Acordamos empezar poco a poco y revisar el costo en junio, para que nadie sienta que cede demasiado?
teaching.explanationEs: Shall we agree to + verbo propone un acuerdo con plazo y deja la decisión al grupo.
segments: Shall we agree to start small and review the cost in
June, so that nobody feels they are giving up too much?

teaching.en: To sum up, we agree on the garden and will review the budget in June, and Mia will report back to the group.
teaching.es: En resumen, estamos de acuerdo con el huerto y revisaremos el presupuesto en junio, y Mia informará al grupo.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up cierra la reunión repitiendo lo acordado, quién hace qué y cuándo.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que hace una propuesta cortés a los vecinos.

choices.text: You must accept a garden by the school, because the plan is fair.
A garden is the only possible option, so let's not waste more time.
I'd like to propose a compromise: a small garden by the school, for a trial year.

feedback.es: I'd like to propose + nombre abre la propuesta con cortesía y la presenta como punto medio; las otras opciones imponen o cierran el debate.

hint.es: Busca la que empieza con I'd like to propose y ofrece un plazo de prueba.

origin.text: At a residents' meeting, you want to suggest a small garden by the school without sounding as if you are giving an order.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es cierto que el plan es difícil, pero es justo.»

feedback.es: Admittedly concede la dificultad antes de defender que el plan es justo.

hint.es: Es el adverbio de concesión que significa «es cierto que».

origin.text: Some neighbours fear that the garden will be expensive. ___, the plan is difficult, but it is fair, because everyone would pay the same.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Podríamos acordar probarlo tres meses y revisar el costo?»

answer.text: Could we agree to try it for three months and review the cost

feedback.es: Could we agree to + verbo propone un acuerdo con plazo y deja abierta la respuesta del grupo.

hint.es: Empieza con Could we agree to.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su jugada en la reunión.

pairs: I'd like to propose a compromise: a market on one Sunday a month.
Admittedly, parking is a problem on market days.
With respect, I see it differently: the noise will not last.
Shall we agree to try it for a month and review the noise?

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una jugada: propone, concede, discrepa con tacto o cierra un acuerdo con plazo.

pairs: I'd like to propose a compromise: a market on one Sunday a month.
Admittedly, parking is a problem on market days.
With respect, I see it differently: the noise will not last.
Shall we agree to try it for a month and review the noise?

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué acuerda finalmente el grupo.

choices.text: To try one concert in June and review the budget afterwards.
To hold weekly concerts but end them at nine.
To cancel the idea until the noise rules change.

feedback.es: Terminar a las nueve fue una sugerencia de Sara; lo que se acuerda es probar un solo concierto en junio y revisar el presupuesto después.

origin.audio: At last night's residents' meeting, Sara proposed a weekly concert in the park. Tom admitted that it was a lovely idea, but he voiced a concern about the noise after ten o'clock. Sara took his point and suggested ending at nine. Mia still had reservations about the cost, so the group agreed to try one concert in June and to review the budget afterwards. Nobody was entirely happy, but everyone left with a plan.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta cortés a una propuesta que no te convence.

choices.text: That is a terrible idea. Nobody wants noise on Fridays.
I like the idea, but I'm a bit worried about the noise. Could we try one evening first?
Fine. Do what you want, but don't expect me to come.

feedback.es: Reconoce la idea, expresa la duda con un atenuador y propone una prueba; las otras respuestas son bruscas o pasivo-agresivas.

origin.text: Tom proposes a concert in the park every Friday. You think it would be too noisy, but you want to keep the atmosphere friendly.

prompt.es: Elige el cierre que resume el acuerdo de la reunión.

choices.text: To sum up, we agree to open a market every day from July and review it next year.
To sum up, we disagree about the market and will not meet again until there is a vote.
To sum up, we agree to try a short market for a month and meet again in July.

feedback.es: To sum up repite lo acordado: un mercado de horario corto, una prueba de un mes y una nueva reunión en julio.

origin.text: After the meeting, the neighbours will start a small market, try it for a month, keep the opening hours short because of the noise, and meet again in July to review the results.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra Mia hacia la objeción de Tom.

choices.text: She respects his objection but gently pushes for a trial.
She ignores his objection because it seems too small.
She agrees with him and drops her proposal.

feedback.es: Acepta su punto («I took your point»), pero sugiere una prueba corta y le pide una mente abierta sin insistir: discrepa con tacto.

origin.audio: Mia listened carefully to Tom's objection about the noise, and then said that she took his point. However, she added that in her experience the complaints usually came from a few households, so she wondered whether a short trial might change his mind. She did not insist; she simply asked him to keep an open mind.

prompt.es: Completa: «La reunión estaba cerca de un punto muerto.»

feedback.es: Deadlock es el bloqueo en el que ninguna parte cede; una concesión mutua lo evita.

origin.text: The two groups could not agree, and the meeting was close to a ___ until Sara suggested that each side give up one demand.

prompt.es: Escribe tu intervención: propón, concede, discrepa con tacto y acuerda.

answer.text: Thank you, everyone. I'd like to propose a compromise: a small street market on the first Sunday of each month, with stalls for local food and plants. It would bring neighbours together and help small businesses. Tom, I take your point: admittedly, a market may be noisy, and we do not have much money. However, I see it a little differently. With respect, I think the noise would last only a few hours, and the stall fees could pay for the cleaning. I'm afraid I cannot agree that the risk is so big. Could we agree to try it for one month and then review the noise and the cost together? Perhaps we could also keep the opening hours short, from ten to two, so that nobody is bothered in the evening. If it does not work, we will stop, and nobody will have lost anything important. To sum up, I propose a one-month trial, a short timetable and a review in November. Shall we say that we start in October and meet again in November? I hope we can reach a consensus tonight.
accepted: Thank you, everyone. I'd like to propose a compromise: a small street market on the first Sunday of each month, with stalls for local food and plants. It would bring neighbours together and help small businesses. Tom, I take your point: admittedly, a market may be noisy, and we do not have much money. However, I see it a little differently. With respect, I think the noise would last only a few hours, and the stall fees could pay for the cleaning. I'm afraid I cannot agree that the risk is so big. Could we agree to try it for one month and then review the noise and the cost together? Perhaps we could also keep the opening hours short, from ten to two, so that nobody is bothered in the evening. If it does not work, we will stop, and nobody will have lost anything important. To sum up, I propose a one-month trial, a short timetable and a review in November. Shall we say that we start in October and meet again in November? I hope we can reach a consensus tonight.

Good evening. I'd like to suggest closing our street to cars on one Sunday a month for a small market. It is true that it could be loud, Tom, and I understand your worry about the budget. Still, I am not sure that the problem is as big as it seems. The stalls would pay a small fee, and volunteers could help clean the street afterwards. What if we agree to a one-month test? Perhaps we could meet again afterwards and decide together whether the market should continue. To sum up, I propose a short trial, a review in November and a decision that everybody can accept. I believe this is fair for everyone, and I hope you agree.

feedback.es: Una buena intervención propone el mercado, concede un punto a Tom, discrepa con tacto y cierra con un acuerdo de prueba concreto y un resumen.

origin.text: Reunión de vecinos. Propones cerrar una calle un domingo al mes para un mercado. Tom cree que habrá demasiado ruido y que faltará dinero. Escribe entre 220 y 270 palabras: propón el mercado, concede un punto a Tom, discrepa con tacto, propón un acuerdo final (prueba de un mes) y cierra resumiendo lo acordado.

evidenceGroups: I would like to put forward
I see it a little differently
I'd like to voice a concern

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere decir en realidad Tom con este comentario?

choices.text: That he fully supports the plan and wants to start tomorrow.
That he has reservations and wants more information before agreeing.
That he wants the teachers to decide where the garden goes.

feedback.es: «In theory», «my only worry» y «perhaps we should hear the teachers first» muestran reservas y la petición de más información antes de decidir.

origin.text: Tom says: “I agree that the garden is a good idea in theory. My only worry is whether the school will really have time to look after it. Perhaps we should hear what the teachers think first.”

prompt.es: Escucha el final de la reunión y elige qué hará Sara.

choices.text: She will buy the paint in May.
She will ask for volunteers to paint the gate.
She will check the budget before anything is ordered.

feedback.es: En el resumen se reparten tareas: Tom compra la pintura, Mia pide voluntarios y Sara revisará el presupuesto antes de hacer pedidos.

origin.audio: To sum up, we agree to paint the gate in May. Tom will buy the paint, Mia will ask for volunteers, and Sara will check the budget before anything is ordered. If the cost turns out to be higher than expected, we will review the plan at the next meeting.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Con todo respeto, me preocupa que el presupuesto sea demasiado ajustado.»

answer.text: With respect I am worried that the budget is too tight

feedback.es: With respect suaviza el desacuerdo y I am worried that… presenta la duda como preocupación, no como ataque.
